defectsFoundAndFixed.whyThisSectionExists: Both defects below were in MY work, and NEITHER was caught by the test suites — both were caught only by the typecheck. The first also passed every test I had written while being functionally dead, so it is written up here rather than quietly corrected.

defect1_missingExport_that_tests_could_n.what: `derive.ts` imported `SETBACK_ADOPTED_DATE_FIELD_KEYS` from `setbackCitationVintage.ts`, but the constant was never EXPORTED there. TS2305.
defect1_missingExport_that_tests_could_n.whyEveryTestPassedAnyway: A missing named import arrives as `undefined`, and `readSetbackDateFromRowAtSource` treats `opts.adoptedKeys: undefined` as 'no adoption keys to read' — it skips the read rather than throwing. So LDT's drawn-envelope path read NO adoption date at all, silently, while all 96 targeted tests passed and the future-effective declaration still appeared (just without its adoption date).
defect1_missingExport_that_tests_could_n.fix: Exported the constant from the module, with the doc comment recording why the adoption field is held to a stricter date standard than the effective date.
defect1_missingExport_that_tests_could_n.regressionTestAdded: `derive.test.ts` gains a P-354 block whose first case asserts the note CONTAINS `adopted 2026-08-11`. That assertion fails on the pre-fix code, because the adoption date was the part being silently dropped.

defect2_test_named_a_basis_that_does_not.what: A new test called `readableBasisOrNull(..., "corpus-row-effective-date")`. That member is NEW IN CORPUS 1.5.0, which is unpublished; legacy-design-tools installs @empressaio/setback-corpus@1.2.0, whose `SetbackDateBasis` is `"ordinance-effective-date" | "corpus-table-effective-date" | "gis-row-citation-ordinance" | "gis-row-edit-date" | "gis-layer-data-last-edit-unattributed" | "atom-source-vintage" | "unreadable"`. TS2345.
defect2_test_named_a_basis_that_does_not.fix: The test now asserts the STATE still reports its basis, using a member that exists, with a comment naming the new member and the 1.5.0 dependency. The assertion is about the state, not the member name, so it holds unchanged when 1.5.0 lands.
defect2_test_named_a_basis_that_does_not.leaveBehind: This is the concrete evidence for the close's leave_behind item on per-repo corpus pins: a consumer cannot even NAME the new basis until its pin moves.

defectsFoundAndFixed.aThirdQuestion_checked_andFoundSafe: After defect1/defect2 the obvious follow-up was whether the same shape-only-date hazard reached the factory and hauska-map, since the factory compares `sourceDate > asOf` lexically. Read and checked: BOTH assign a source date only after their own calendar-validating check (`isStrictIsoDate`, which rejects roll-overs via an ISO round-trip), so the comparison always compares real dates. The hazard was real ONLY in legacy-design-tools, whose reader deliberately inherits the corpus's shape-only tolerance — see defect3.

defect3_foundAndFixed_shapeOnlyDateWasPr.what: My first implementation of `applyFutureEffectiveState` in legacy-design-tools compared `read.sourceDate <= asOf` lexically. Because LDT's reader inherits the corpus's SHAPE-ONLY notion of a date, the value `2026-13-99` read as `read` with `sourceDate: "2026-13-99"`, which is lexically greater than `2026-09-18`, so it was promoted to `future-effective` and the customer sentence became 'Setback rule takes effect 2026-13-99 — the rule is served ahead of its effective date…'. A nonsense date asserted to a customer as a legal fact.
defect3_foundAndFixed_shapeOnlyDateWasPr.caughtBy: legacy-design-tools' own pre-existing test `INHERITS THE CORPUS'S SHAPE-ONLY NOTION OF A DATE, deliberately, rather than being stricter than the resolver`, which pins `citationVintage` to null for that input. THIS IS THE ONE DEFECT THE TEST SUITE CAUGHT.
defect3_foundAndFixed_shapeOnlyDateWasPr.theDistinctionThatWasMissing: 'Is this a date?' and 'has this date arrived?' are different questions. The corpus's shape-only reader answers the first, deliberately, because it ORDERS candidates by date and `2026-13-99` sorts sensibly. The second has no answer for a value that is not a real calendar date. My code conflated them.
defect3_foundAndFixed_shapeOnlyDateWasPr.fix: The promotion now requires the date to be a real calendar date (shape + ISO round-trip, so roll-overs fail too). A shape-only value stays `read`: it is still SERVED as the effective date and no unreadable declaration is made about it — which preserves the ruling the existing test pins — but no arrival is asserted.
defect3_foundAndFixed_shapeOnlyDateWasPr.alsoFixed: `readableBasisOrNull` only recognised `read`, so a future-effective date — which WAS read, and whose basis is therefore known — reported no basis. Now recognises both.
defect3_foundAndFixed_shapeOnlyDateWasPr.regressionTestsAdded: Six in `setbackCitationVintage.test.ts` (both directions: a real future date promotes and names both dates; an in-force date is untouched; asOf == effectiveDate reads `read`; `2026-13-99` is NOT promoted and publishes nothing; `2026-02-31` is not promoted either; an unreadable read is never promoted) and five in `derive.test.ts` over the district-ROW path (row asked first; row date beats table; no-row-date falls back to the table unchanged as the paired control; an in-force row date publishes nothing; a shape-only row date prints no nonsense).

sourceQuotes.effectiveDate: Read verbatim from the rewrite's own Section 1.09 'Effective Date' in source PDF 'Unified Development Code 8.11.2026.pdf', p.26 of 485 (the PDF each rewrite row's own `citation_url` carries): 'This Code shall become effective November 1, 2026, and be in full force and effect in accordance with the City Charter.'
sourceQuotes.adoptedDate: 2026-08-11, the Council adoption already recorded in the table's own notes and in the source PDF's filename (8.11.2026). STATED HONESTLY: a full-text search of the rewrite PDF body found NO adoption-ordinance line for the UDC itself — the only 'adopted on <date>' matches are Historic Overlay District ordinances (pp.125-127) — so this date rests on the council action as already recorded, NOT on a quotable line inside the document. The effective date, by contrast, is quotable and quoted above. Both facts are written into the table's note so a later reader cannot mistake the weaker provenance for the stronger one.
sourceQuotes.theAmendingSupplementTrap: The note above the rows records that the text was 'codified through Ordinance No. 2025-54 adopted September 9, 2025'. That is the SUPPLEMENT's adoption, not any row's effective date, and it is deliberately NOT promoted to a row date: promoting it would put a current row into a most-current-wins comparison on evidence that does not exist. Recorded in the addendum so the reasoning outlives this session.
